subject: POC load portrait & acceptance pathway with Lumera
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@lumera.ai>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC load portrait & acceptance pathway with Lumera

Hi Evan — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth heading into the trial: 

Summary of ask
- Goal: validate Redwood inference integration for Lumera Assistant MVP (text generation + conversation state).
- Primary success metrics: 99thpct tail latency < 350ms for single-turn text generation at 1–2 tokens/ms (median token length ~18), and throughput across sustained window of 500 RPS with 200 concurrent sessions during peak bursts.

Workload profile (from call) — please confirm:
- Typical request size: 120–350 tokens (prompt + context).
- Median token length per request: ~18 tokens for short queries; some long contextual requests up to 600 tokens.
- Expected average RPS during POC: 120 RPS baseline, target test windows at 500 RPS for 15–30 minutes.
- Concurrency: 80–220 (concurrent active sessions), bursts up to 800 RPS for <5 minutes during simulated traffic spikes.

Acceptance criteria (proposed)
1) Performance: 99th percentile latency under 350ms for single-turn gen on the selected model variant during a 30-minute steady-state test at 500 RPS.
2) Accuracy/regressions: no more than 3% drop in top-line response-safety or hallucination checks vs. your control set (we'll run your eval harness).
3) Cost envelope: tokens/unit economics estimate within the forecast range — Redwood to provide cost estimate given observed token mixes.
4) Observability: access to per-request traces + token-level cost breakdown for the trial period.

Deliverables and timeline
- Today: Lumera to share representative sample payloads and the eval prompt set (Evan — you mentioned a sample bundle).
- By Wed (2027-09-15): Redwood will provide a draft POC plan + SLA doc and a first-pass traffic ingestion schema.
- Week of 09/20: baseline tests + one spike window; mid-week readout and tuning.
- Week of 09/27: final acceptance run and handoff to your platform team.

Owners at Redwood (suggested)
- Naomi Feldman — POC lead / sales (primary contact)
- Dev Patel — infra & benchmarking owner (setup load harness, config)
- Marissa Cole — evaluation & success metrics (runs evals, compiles readout)

Attachments: I attached a quick traffic-capture-schema.csv template and a sample payload bundle to accelerate onboarding.

Please confirm the workload numbers above and whether the success criteria look reasonable. If yes, Evan, can you send the sample payloads and the eval prompt set?

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

--
Attachment: traffic-capture-schema.csv (CSV stub, fields: timestamp, session_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, model, features)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: dev.patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: POC load portrait & acceptance pathway with Lumera (internal)

Folks — forwarding Evan's verbal confirmations from the call and my recap above. Core asks for infra + eval:

Immediate asks for Dev
- Stand up a sandbox target with the model variant we discussed (quantized v1.3) and enable token-level tracing.
- Prepare load harness capable of: steady-state 500 RPS, and scripted spike to 800 RPS for 5 minutes. Include concurrency shaping to simulate 80–220 active sessions.
- Default latency SLO for the run: 99th < 350ms. Capture CPU/GPU utilization and per-shard queuing.

For Marissa
- Prep the eval harness and the control prompt set Evan will send. We'll need accuracy/regression scripts (safety checks + hallucination metrics).

For Aditya
- Can you draft a short notes section for the POC-SLA doc describing rollback behaviour and fallback model variants (cheaper quantized fallback + cross-region fallback) — one paragraph each.

Timeline: target initial sandboxes ready by end of day 2027-09-15 so we can schedule the baseline test on 09/20.

Let me know if any of the workload numbers are unrealistic on our side.

—Naomi

From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@lumera.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@lumera.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC load portrait & acceptance pathway with Lumera

Thanks Naomi — that recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- Sample payloads: attached lumera_mvp_sample_payloads.json — contains representative short and long-session traces (we have ~18k distinct prompt templates).
- Eval set: I'll upload the prompt/eval harness to your Drive link by EOD 9/14.
- Success targets: the 99th <350ms is firm for the MVP flows; for long-context requests (>=400 tokens) we expect higher tail latency but would like linear scaling guidance.

One additional metric: sustained 95th pct latency under 250ms during the 30-minute steady-state would be highly preferred for our user experience. If we can show that on the chosen model variant, adoption increases substantially.

We're comfortable starting the baseline test 09/20 and scheduling a 30-minute acceptance window on 09/28.

Evan Liu
CTO, Lumera AI
evan.liu@lumera.ai

--
Attachment: lumera_mvp_sample_payloads.json (JSON sample bundle, 12KB)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC load portrait & acceptance pathway with Lumera

Thanks — I've started the sandbox spin-up. Quick notes and outstanding questions: 

- Infra plan: provisioning one dedicated GPU pool (4 x A100 equivalent), with dynamic batching tuned for median token length ~18. We'll enable prefix KV cache for repeated conversation contexts.
- Load harness: using wrk + custom token-aware client to replay sample payloads. I'll parameterize runs: baseline 120 RPS (30m), steady 500 RPS (30m), spike 800 RPS (5m).
- Observability: traces will be pushed to the shared Drive folder and to our tracing UI. I'll add token-level cost columns.

Open questions:
1) Do we have an agreed model variant and quantization? Naomi, Evan asked for "quantized v1.3" on the call — is that the model we plan to run?
2) Can Marissa confirm the eval harness will be ready by EOD 09/15 so we can ingest it into the harness?

I'll post the sandbox endpoint and a small readme once ready (ETA: EOD 09/15).

- Dev

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@lumera.ai>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC load portrait & acceptance pathway with Lumera — agreed next steps

Evan — thanks for the samples and clarity. Quick confirmed plan and ownership so we can lock calendars: 

Agreed test plan
- 09/15: Redwood sandbox endpoint published (Dev).
- 09/20: Baseline run (120 RPS, 30m) — internal readout same day.
- 09/23: Tuning window + configuration changes (if needed).
- 09/28: Acceptance window (steady 500 RPS for 30m; spike 800 RPS for 5m). Goal: 99th < 350ms; 95th < 250ms preferred for the MVP flows.

Acceptance criteria (finalized)
- Performance: 99th < 350ms on MVP flows during acceptance window; 95th < 250ms preferred.
- Functional/regression: <3% degradation on your control eval set.
- Observability & cost: access to traces + per-token cost CSV for the acceptance window.

Action items
- Evan: confirm the drive upload and share any special load corner-cases you want simulated (e.g., multi-turn resets, truncated contexts).
- Dev: post sandbox endpoint and README by EOD 09/15.
- Marissa: confirm eval harness ingestion by EOD 09/15; provide the first-pass regression dashboard by 09/22.
- Aditya: draft two short paragraphs for the POC-SLA (fallbacks + rollback) by 09/16.

I've attached a one-page POC-SLA draft (poc-sla-draft.pdf) for initial review. Evan — if you're happy, let's lock the acceptance window on 09/28 13:00–13:45 PT.

Best,
Naomi

--
